description: White stone cut with a frost-rune that keeps its edge, and nothing anyone has ever broken was carrying it.
lore: A soulstone cannot be worked. Not scribed, not faceted, not ground down; the trade established that early and expensively, and a setter's whole art is holding a stone fast without altering it by a scratch. Which leaves an awkward question standing over this one, because there is a frost-rune on it.

Nobody put it there. Take one to a window: no tooling anywhere, no bench marks, no chatter in the strokes, and the white star does not lie on the surface. It goes in. It is still going at the middle, and its edges are as sharp as the hour it dropped out of a broken shape into somebody's hand. It is not a mark made on a stone. It is the shape of the thing all the way down, the way plates are the shape of the plated ones. Something is a frost-rune the way a hedgehog is spines, and what it does is entirely in character: whatever it touches runs late.

[[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]] asks. He maps ground that will not hold still and is used to figures that refuse to add up, so for years he has put two questions to every seller holding one — where did this come from, who had it before you — and written the answers down. Thirty-one entries. Plotted, they make a scatter with no centre, right across the valley, thinning toward nowhere, which is not the shape a creature's range makes on a sheet. He was asked at a fire once whether he thought there was one out there. He said a scatter with no centre is what you get when you map a thing being handed about rather than found, and did not say the next sentence.
gm_notes: Unbound stone number three, and the coldest handling of the three: the oddity is not the absence of a creature but the presence of a mark, on a substance that provably cannot be marked. Shipped line said the creature was 'still out there somewhere, unmet' — replaced, because that is the comfortable answer and the question is better open. Gunnar's thirty-one entries exist as a physical page he has shown to no one, and the sentence he declined to say is not written down anywhere either. Do not resolve it; the Made-leaves-a-stone argument belongs to the sunburst record and must not be re-run here.
